description:
Advances: ancora.findings

Severity: High (calibrated; critical review 2026-09-05, consolidated finding CF8, consensus spec+data). Evidence: with two overrides: entries for the same subject and code, one subject-wide and one requirement:-scoped, the effective severity is decided by YAML list order (lib/ancora/config.ex override_for); reversing the entries flips the result between :off and :error. No statement in ancora.findings defines a precedence. Question to decide: does a requirement:-scoped entry beat a subject-wide entry for the same subject and code (specificity), or is it an error to declare both? Then state it, implement it, and test both orders. Ready-for: implement.

## Investigation contract, 2026-09-07

Evidence and corrections:
Report: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/04-report.md
Measurements: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/03-measurements.md
Source revision: 82c2ca8329e1303ececc610dfc9f72986b96c84a. This contract proposes work; no implementation is claimed.

Deliverable:
Within the config layer, match exact subject+requirement+code before subject+code fallback, regardless of list order. Reject duplicate equal-specificity selectors with config/invalid_value and ignore every entry in the ambiguous group, rather than choosing the first; apply remaining valid policy normally. Distinct requirement selectors remain independent. Preserve config-off absorption, trailer downgrade and acknowledgment precedence after selecting config policy. Document this in the findings contract.

Verification:
- Replay override_order in both permutations: exact requirement resolves to info in both, while an unrelated requirement receives the subject-wide error.
- Cover exact off against subject error, exact error against subject off, missing requirement, equal-selector duplicates in both orders, and separate requirements. Assert diagnostics and severity_source, not just exit status.
- A consumer config reorder alone must produce zero verdict or count changes.
- Cadence: focused tests during implementation; at final verification run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix test, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused and mix spec.check against the actual integration base. CI must pass both configured Elixir/OTP combinations. Record evidence of the described symptom after the consuming release before claiming it done.

Allowed touches:
lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/ancora/severity.ex, corresponding tests, ancora.findings spec and its decision amendment.

Out of Scope (files):
Unrelated production modules, credentials, dependencies and consumer repositories. Release metadata belongs to release preparation.

Out of Scope (intent):
No new general policy language, trailer precedence redesign, or blanket severity reduction.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Focused negative and positive behavior fixtures pass.
- [ ] Affected specs and decisions describe the actual changed behavior.
- [ ] Full repository CI and spec gate pass without cosmetic acknowledgment edits.

Decision:
Specificity expresses the existing requirement selector purpose. Rejecting coexistence would force adopters to enumerate all remaining requirements; first-match behavior demonstrably changes verdict on a YAML reorder.

Open Questions:
None. Unmeasured consumer replay and release behavior are explicit Verification obligations, not claimed results.
